title: Databases on AWS: RDS and DynamoDB

questions.prompt: What is the difference between RDS Multi-AZ and a read replica?

options.text: Multi-AZ is a synchronous standby for automatic failover (availability); a read replica is asynchronous and used to scale reads
They are the same feature with different names
Multi-AZ scales reads; read replicas provide failover
Both are only for backups

questions.explanation: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover and is not readable. Read replicas are asynchronous copies used to scale read traffic (and can be cross-Region).

options.text: A serverless NoSQL key-value/document store with single-digit-ms latency, designed around access patterns
A managed relational database with joins and SQL
A virtual server you patch yourself
An object storage service

questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database (key-value and document) with single-digit-millisecond latency and automatic scaling; you model tables around access patterns and there are no joins.

questions.prompt: When should you choose a relational database (RDS) over DynamoDB?

options.text: When you need joins, ad-hoc queries, and ACID transactions across related tables
When you want to avoid managing capacity at massive scale
When you only ever look up items by a single key
Never — DynamoDB is always better

questions.explanation: Relational engines fit structured, related data needing joins, flexible queries, and transactions. DynamoDB fits simple key-based access at large scale.

questions.prompt: Which tasks does a managed database like RDS handle for you? Select all that apply.

options.text: Patching the database engine and OS
Automated backups
Automatic failover with Multi-AZ
Designing your data model and access rules

questions.explanation: RDS manages patching, backups, and failover. You still design the data model and control access — that stays your responsibility.

questions.prompt: In DynamoDB, each item is identified by a primary key consisting of a ____ key (and an optional sort key).
questions.explanation: A DynamoDB primary key is a partition key, optionally combined with a sort key; you design tables around how you'll query by these keys.

questions.prompt: Do you get operating-system access to an Amazon RDS instance?

options.text: Yes, full SSH access like EC2
No — RDS is managed, so you interact through the database, not the OS
Only on weekends
Only for MySQL

questions.explanation: RDS is a managed service: AWS runs the host and engine, so there's no OS access — a trade-off for AWS handling patching and maintenance.
